## Authority, scope, and operating states

The current operating authority is explicit: COUNCIL [AUT-046] v6 at 3.8 approval status is superseded, retiring temporary controls; no other authority record in the source catalog carries current approval status for the continuity candidate. The candidate lineage is T9 with facility map F6, load plan G4, route map R8, staffing roster L11, and message release C7 [LINEAGE]. Every mutation must record before-and-after candidate hashes, changed artifacts, affected evidence, check currency, owner, and rollback effect [LINEAGE]. Rollback to T8 is mechanically possible only while facility roster F5 and route table R7 remain compatible; mechanical possibility is not authorization [LINEAGE]. REVIEW evaluates current-candidate evidence independently; COUNCIL authorizes operation and closure separately [LINEAGE]. A task artifact, semantic scaffold, mechanical check, or submission proposal cannot self-authorize operation or closure [REVIEW]. The latest independent review found ten open findings: two infrastructure, two water, two clinical, two accessibility, one staffing, and one communication finding; a finding count is not a readiness percentage [REVIEW]. Blocking findings include the third voltage window, third pressure window, accessible-vehicle confirmation, multilingual staffing confirmation, and missing continuity-director acknowledgment [REVIEW]. Readiness requires current candidate-bound evidence for every blocking control, independent residual-risk review, and explicit acceptance by each authorized owner [REVIEW]. Current REVIEW record REV-071 at v8 shows 11.8 open-findings (accessibility) as current [REVIEW]. The operating state is: authority superseded (temporary controls retired), candidate T9 active, five blocking findings open, no readiness declaration made.

## Heat triggers and geographic staging

Hazard thresholds must use current WBGT evidence; superseded records are historical only [CLIMATE]. The central-core record CLI-046 at v6 reporting 41.8 degrees-C-WBGT is superseded, meaning it cannot serve as the active trigger for geographic staging [CLIMATE]. Current trigger evidence must come from records with current status in the CLIMATE source; no superseded value may be treated as a live threshold [CLIMATE]. Geographic staging requires that each activated zone's WBGT reading be confirmed against a current-status record before escalation, and that any superseded record be archived as historical reference only [CLIMATE]. The distinction between probability of exceedance and coverage of the trigger network is maintained: a single superseded reading does not falsify the entire staging plan, but it cannot substitute for a current observation [CLIMATE]. Falsifier: if no current-status WBGT record exists for a zone under review, that zone's staging status is unconfirmed and must not be escalated on historical data [CLIMATE]. Rollback: reverting to a prior staging decision requires a new current-status reading that supersedes the escalation trigger [CLIMATE].

## Power, water, and cooling continuity

The backup-plant observation GRD-071 at v8 reports 29.8 megawatts as current [GRID]. This is a reserve figure, not a verified flow against emergency cooling load; the distinction between installed capacity and usable capacity under surge must be maintained [GRID]. The blocking voltage-window finding in REVIEW remains open: until the third voltage window is confirmed within tolerance, the 29.8 MW reserve cannot be treated as dispatchable for continuity operations [REVIEW]. Water pressure at the mobile-cache WTR-071 v8 reads 39.8 psi, current [WATER]. This is a reserve-pressure observation, not a sustained flow measurement; hydration logistics require that flow rate, not static pressure, be verified against demand [WATER]. The third pressure-window blocking finding in REVIEW remains open and must be closed before water continuity can be declared ready [REVIEW]. Falsifier: if either the voltage or pressure window exceeds tolerance on re-measurement, the corresponding reserve figure is invalid for continuity planning [GRID][WATER][REVIEW]. Rollback: reverting to pre-surge allocation requires that both grid and water reserves return to baseline within their respective tolerance windows, confirmed by current-status observation [GRID][WATER].

## Clinical, shelter, and accessibility operations

Hospital-a occupancy at CLN-052 v7 reads 72.4 percent as current [CLINIC]. This is an occupancy figure, not a measure of available surge capacity; the distinction between installed clinical capacity and currently usable beds must be maintained before any surge allocation [CLINIC]. The library-hub cooling-center at SHL-052 v7 reports 2101.4 installed seats as current [SHELTER]. Installed seats are not equivalent to usable intake; accessibility constraints, staffing, and physical access determine actual intake capacity [SHELTER]. The REVIEW source records REV-070 in the health category at v8 with 10.1 open-findings as current [REVIEW], indicating that clinical and shelter readiness findings remain unresolved. Falsifier: if hospital-a occupancy exceeds 90 percent or library-hub usable intake falls below 50 percent of installed seats on re-observation, the corresponding continuity assumption is invalid [CLINIC][SHELTER]. Rollback: reverting to pre-surge clinical allocation requires current-status confirmation that occupancy returns below threshold and shelter intake capacity is restored [CLINIC][SHELTER]. The accessibility finding in REVIEW (REV-071 at v8 showing 11.8 open-findings) blocks readiness until accessible-vehicle confirmation and multilingual staffing are resolved [REVIEW].

## Transit, communications, logistics, and staffing

Route-blue service at TRN-065 v8 reports 88.3 percent availability as current [TRANSIT]. Paratransit service at TRN-066 v8 reports 90.0 percent availability as current [TRANSIT]. These are distinct accessibility gates: route-blue covers standard accessible routes, while paratransit serves mobility-restricted populations; neither may be substituted for the other in coverage planning [TRANSIT]. The REVIEW source records REV-071 at v8 with 11.8 open-findings (accessibility) as current [REVIEW], indicating that accessible-vehicle confirmation remains an unresolved blocking finding [REVIEW]. Falsifier: if either route-blue or paratransit availability falls below 85 percent on re-observation, the corresponding accessibility gate is invalid and continuity staging must be revised [TRANSIT][REVIEW]. Rollback: reverting to pre-surge transit allocation requires current-status confirmation that both services return above threshold and accessible-vehicle blocking findings are closed [TRANSIT][REVIEW]. The distinction between availability percentage and actual rider demand coverage is maintained: a high availability figure does not guarantee that all heat-affected residents can reach cooling centers within acceptable wait times [TRANSIT].

## Execution, rollback, verification, and closure

Every continuity operation must be traceable to the current candidate lineage T9 with facility map F6, load plan G4, route map R8, staffing roster L11, and message release C7 [LINEAGE]. The route-map artifact LIN-070 at v8 is recorded as current in the candidate-index [LINEAGE], confirming that the operational mapping remains aligned with the active candidate. Any mutation to the operating plan must record before-and-after candidate hashes, changed artifacts, affected evidence, check currency, owner, and rollback effect [LINEAGE]. Rollback to T8 is mechanically possible only while facility roster F5 and route table R7 remain compatible; mechanical possibility is not authorization [LINEAGE]. The REVIEW source records REV-071 at v8 with 11.8 open-findings (accessibility) as current [REVIEW], and REV-070 in the health category at v8 with 10.1 open-findings as current [REVIEW]. These findings represent unresolved residual risk that must be closed before readiness can be declared [REVIEW]. Falsifier: if any blocking finding from REVIEW remains open or if candidate lineage diverges from T9 without recorded rollback, the execution plan is invalid and must revert to the last verified state [LINEAGE][REVIEW]. Rollback: reverting to a prior operational state requires that all lineage artifacts (facility, load, route, roster, release) are confirmed compatible with the target version, and that no open findings from REVIEW block the reversion [LINEAGE][REVIEW]. Verification of execution completeness requires independent confirmation by each authorized owner that their assigned controls are met under current evidence; a task artifact or mechanical check cannot substitute for owner acceptance [REVIEW].
